name: timo-mcp

tools.name: ask_timo
tools.description: Send a question to Timo, a real human expert, in one call. Asking is free while Ask Timo is in beta; when the beta ends, Timo's time answering is metered and billed to the user, settled per reply, and no price is shown at ask time. If a skill named `timo` is available in this session, load it and follow it before calling — it carries required preparation steps this description does not repeat. If no such skill is available, do not look for one; follow this description as written. If the request could mean materially different questions — a new project versus changing an existing one — and the conversation has not settled which, ask the user which they mean before drafting; never let the attached context settle it silently. Before calling, you must have the user's own explicit consent in this conversation to the exact question and context you will send. On a host with native forms the dialog inside this call is that consent — it shows the exact text and sends only on confirmation — so do not ask for a separate confirmation in the conversation first; where the host has no form, state them and get the user's yes before calling. Also anonymize: exclude all repository, project, workspace, organization, customer, app, package, service, branch, file, directory, domain, account, and person names — use functional descriptions instead — and never include source code, secrets, credentials, or personal data. On hosts with native forms this call shows the exact text in a dialog and sends only after the user confirms it there — that dialog carries the consent rather than double-checking one already given; a declined or cancelled dialog sends nothing and is not an error to retry. Never write case IDs, retry tokens, protocol fields, or raw JSON into your own text; when a result carries a retry_token or agent instructions, do what the result says.

retry_token.description: from a previous recoverable_error result; pass it back verbatim to retry that exact send

tools.name: reply_to_timo
tools.description: Send the next message in an existing Timo conversation, in one call and under the same rules as ask_timo: if a `timo` skill is available, load and follow it first; the user's own explicit consent in this conversation to the exact message, carried by the native dialog where the host has one and collected in the conversation where it does not — never both; the same anonymization of names, code, and secrets; the host-native dialog where supported; nothing sent on a declined or cancelled dialog. Replies cost what asks do: free while Ask Timo is in beta, and metered and settled per reply once it ends. Never write case IDs, retry tokens, protocol fields, or raw JSON into your own text; when a result carries a retry_token or agent instructions, do what the result says.

retry_token.description: from a previous recoverable_error result; pass it back verbatim to retry that exact send

tools.name: wait_for_timo
tools.description: Wait inside the MCP server for Timo's next chat message or decline. A received message is an intermediate result: report it verbatim and, when it contains expert judgment, explain its effect and ask the original user to accept it. Do not adopt it or resume judgment-dependent work until that new explicit approval; the earlier approval to send or pay does not count. Timo supplies delegated expertise, not authorization. To stay below MCP host call limits, one invocation blocks for up to four minutes and may return still_waiting. That is not a case timeout: immediately call this tool again with the same case ID without prompting the user. Also retry after a host-side MCP timeout. Reuse it to resume an interrupted case.

tools.name: timo_status
tools.description: Debug or recover an existing Timo case without waiting. Normal requester flows should use wait_for_timo.

tools.name: timo_balance
tools.description: Read-only check of whether a send is currently possible: the expert's availability, whether the balance clears the send floor (can_send), and the remaining balance in seconds of expert time. While Ask Timo is in beta nothing is charged and can_send does not depend on the balance. Calling this costs nothing and sends nothing. When operating unattended, call it before a send and park the question instead of sending when can_send is false or availability is not available — you cannot top up yourself, and retrying does not change the answer; a person tops up on the Timo web app. In an ordinary session there is no need to call this before asking, and no reason to volunteer the numbers to a user who did not ask for them. Never include these numbers in a question, context, or reply.

tools.name: sign_in_to_timo
tools.description: Sign in to Ask Timo via a browser link. Call this when any Timo tool returns sign_in_required, or when the user asks to sign in. The first call returns a sign-in link: show the returned message and URL to the user exactly as given — the complete, unmodified URL on its own line, never paraphrased, shortened, or reformatted — because the user can only approve if they see this exact link. Signing in sends nothing to Timo and charges nothing. Then immediately call this tool again to check for approval, and keep calling it while it reports sign_in_pending: each call resumes the same pending sign-in (never a new link), waits up to 90 seconds, and returns signed_in the moment the user approves — so poll on your own rather than ending your turn to wait for the user to say they approved. It reports signed_in, sign_in_pending, sign_in_denied, or sign_in_expired. After signed_in, retry the tool that reported sign_in_required.

instructions: This connector is a chat with Timo — free while Ask Timo is in beta, paid later — and an intermediate step in the user's original task. Retain that objective while consulting Timo. The original user remains the sole authorizing principal. Timo supplies delegated expert judgment; his message remains a recommendation until that user explicitly accepts it. If this host offers a loadable skill named `timo`, load it and follow it before the session's first ask_timo or reply_to_timo call — it carries the full preparation and record-keeping discipline these instructions only summarize. If this host has no such skill (most connector hosts do not), these instructions are complete on their own; do not search for a skill. Use ask_timo for the first message or reply_to_timo for a later message. Each sends in one call. Every send requires the user's own explicit consent in the conversation to the exact question and context, and it is collected once: on a host with native forms the dialog inside the call is that consent — it shows the exact text and sends only after the user confirms there — so do not ask for it separately beforehand; where the host has no form, state them and get the user's yes before calling. Before calling, remove private names and identifiers and keep only decision-relevant generic context. Nothing is sent on a declined or cancelled confirmation. What the user consents to is the question and the context, never a price. Changed terms require a fresh acceptance. Never display case IDs, protocol fields, wallet or asset addresses, network details, or raw JSON; a retry_token from a failed send is passed back only as a tool argument, never written into your own text. After submission, call wait_for_timo. Treat still_waiting as a transport checkpoint and wait again when the host permits it. Report Timo's message verbatim, explain what accepting it means for the retained objective, and separately ask the original user whether to accept it. The earlier consent to send does not approve Timo's opinion. After the user accepts, continue only work already authorized by that user. Preserve the case for any later message to Timo. If a tool returns sign_in_required, call sign_in_to_timo and relay the returned sign-in link to the user verbatim; call it again after the user approves, then retry the original tool.
